body.p: Claims 1-2, 5-12, and 15-20 are pending in this application. Claims 1, 2, 7, 11, 12, and 17 have been amended, without waiver. Claims 3, 4, 13, and 14 are cancelled, without waiver. Reconsideration and further examination are respectfully requested.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over McMillan [US 20200339266 Al] in view of Hera [EP 3106343 Al],

Applicant respectfully traverses each rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103. To establish prima facie obviousness of a claimed invention, all the claim limitations must be taught or suggested by the prior art. In re Ryoka, 180 U.S.P.Q. 580 (C.C.P.A. 1974). See also In re Wilson, 165 U.S.P.Q. 494 (C.C.P.A. 1970).

Moreover, "[o]bviousness can only be established by combining or modifying the teachings of the prior art to produce the claimed invention where there is some teaching, suggestion, or motivation to do so found either explicitly or implicitly in the references themselves or the knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art." MPEP § 2143.01. "If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious." MPEP § 2143.03, citing In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071, 5 USPQ 2d 1596 (Fed. Cir. 1988).

In an effort to expedite prosecution, the Applicant has amended Claim 1. Support for this amendment is found throughout the as-filed application, such as Claims 2, 3, and 4. Applicant respectfully submits amended Claim 1 recites elements which have not been disclosed, taught or suggested by the cited references.
McMillan and Hera fail to disclose, teach, or suggest "the one or more sensors are configured for distinguishable detection of a user input, wherein the

user input includes each of a user touch, press, and hold," and "transmit one or more feedback signals to one or more feedback devices in response to a user touch" and "wherein the one or more feedback devices include the output jack" which is "integrated into the control panel" (emphasis added) as recited in amended Claim 1. Rather, arguendo at best, the sensing of McMillan is touch screen sensors associated with the PED for detecting user selections. McMillan does not distinguish between a touch and a press. Applicant's disclosure allows a single button to be touched, without pressing, to hear "an auditory message indicating the feature associated with the one or more buttons". This may aide blind individuals and provide a means for knowing what buttons do before pressing them, without needing braille bumps added to the buttons.
Claim 1 is believed to be allowable for at least these reasons.
Claims 2, and 5-10 depend upon Claim 1 directly or indirectly and are allowable based on their dependence upon an allowable base claim.

For at least the reasons Claim 1 is believed allowable, it is believed that independent Claim 11 is allowable. Claims 12, and 15-20 depend upon Claim 11 directly or indirectly and are allowable based on their dependence upon an allowable base claim.

Applicant respectfully traverses all the arguments made in the Office Action that were not specifically addressed above. The fact that rejections and/or statements may not be explicitly addressed during the course of prosecution should not be taken as an admission of any sort, and Applicant hereby reserves any and all rights to contest such rejections and/or statements at a later time.

Applicant may have cancelled and/or amended one or more claims during the course of prosecution. Claims have been amended and/or cancelled in this Amendment solely to facilitate expeditious prosecution. Applicant notes that any such cancellations and/or amendments will have transpired (i) prior to issuance and (ii) in the context of the rules that govern claim interpretation during

prosecution before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (Patent Office). Applicant notes that the rules that govern claim interpretation during prosecution form a radically different context than the rules that govern claim interpretation subsequent to a patent issuing. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that any cancellations and/or amendments during the course of prosecution should be held to be tangential to and/or unrelated to patentability in the event that such cancellations and/or amendments are viewed in a post-issuance context under post-issuance claim interpretation rules. Applicant submits that support for these amendments may be found in the disclosure as originally filed, and therefore no new matter has been added.

Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue claims as presented prior to this Amendment and additional claims in one or more continuing applications. With respect to any cancelled claims, such cancelled claims were and continue to be a part of the original and/or present patent application(s). Applicant hereby reserves all rights to present any cancelled claim or claims for examination at a later time in this or another application. Applicant hereby gives public notice that any cancelled claims are still to be considered as present in all related patent application(s) (e.g. the original and/or present patent application) for all appropriate purposes (e.g., written description and/or enablement). Applicant does not intend to dedicate the subject matter of any cancelled claims to the public.

In light of the forgoing, reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims is earnestly solicited. Should the Examiner have any questions or comments concerning the foregoing, Applicant's attorney welcomes the opportunity to discuss the same with the Examiner via a telephonic interview.
